reviews.reasoning: All three curly-quoted WEB clauses in this row pass check_web_quotes verbatim with in-field web: refs. The one original-language claim is the imperative inside the quotation at 90:3: spliced from oshb:Ps.90.3 (= web:Ps.90.3) the form is שׁ֣וּבוּ - a prefix-less plural imperative, byte tier at collate, and that skeleton spelling occurs in 1 verse of Ps 90 (sweep --skel, unit = verses: 12 book-wide, Ps.90.3 the only one in this psalm). Span coherence checked from the bytes: 90:4 keeps Yahweh as addressee (בְּֽעֵינֶ֗יךָ, oshb:Ps.90.4 = web:Ps.90.4) and 90:6 closes the grass image (לָ֝עֶ֗רֶב יְמוֹלֵ֥ל וְיָבֵֽשׁ, oshb:Ps.90.6 = web:Ps.90.6), rendered “In the morning it sprouts and springs up. By evening, it is withered and dry.” (web:Ps.90.6); the next verse opens a causal clause. Tiling within Ps 90 is exact at 17 of 17 verses, no gaps or overlaps. check_universals flags the rejected_alternative's no-break phrase as an unswept universal, but it is a four-verse segmentation statement re-derivable by inspection (2ms addressee continuous across 90:4-6), not a count claim - an observation, not a defect. Confidence medium is calibrated for a span whose internal seam at 90:4|90:5 is arguable.

The span is defensible and its WEB quotes are verbatim, but both stated substrate signals fail when re-derived from the pointed text. The unit's own close at 90:12 is asserted to be pre-imperative; MT 90:12 carries כֵּ֣ן הוֹדַ֑ע (oshb:Ps.90.12 = web:Ps.90.12), an imperative addressed to Yahweh, which WEB also renders imperatively. The opening driver is the causal particle at 90:7 (כִּֽי כָלִ֥ינוּ, oshb:Ps.90.7 = web:Ps.90.7) - real, but verse-initial in 3 verses of Ps 90, one of them inside the preceding span, so it does not discriminate this seam, and the row quotes no Hebrew for it. The K/Q verse inside this span is handled safely: of the 65 K/Q verses book-wide in pmarks, MT Ps.90.8 is the only one in Ps 90-91 (the unpointed ketiv stands inline before the pointed qere in the bytes) and the row quotes no Hebrew from 90:8, so no disclosure is owed. The seam at 90:12|90:13 is shared: the unit running 90:13-17 reads the fresh imperative at 90:13 correctly, so the false contrast here has to be repaired without disturbing that reading.

reviews.reasoning: Numbering: web_mt_offset_map gives Ps 91 rule identity, web_title false, 16 verses in both witnesses, so the row's bare web: refs need no dual-cite and citation_sweep is GREEN. The participle claim is byte-true: יֹ֭שֵׁב opens oshb:Ps.91.1 (= web:Ps.91.1), a qotel-pattern form with no prefixed subject marker, matching WEB “He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High” (web:Ps.91.1) - a generic figure, not an addressed you. The first-person confession at 91:2 is equally byte-true (אֹמַ֗ר לַֽ֭יהוָה מַחְסִ֣י and אֶבְטַח בּֽוֹ, oshb:Ps.91.2 = web:Ps.91.2), rendered “I will say of Yahweh,” (web:Ps.91.2). The WEB punctuation claim checks out in the verse bytes, and the warrant does not rest on punctuation alone: the 2ms address genuinely opens at 91:3, whose verb carries a 2ms object suffix (כִּ֤י ה֣וּא יַ֭צִּֽילְךָ, oshb:Ps.91.3 = web:Ps.91.3), rendered “For he will deliver you from the snare of the fowler,” (web:Ps.91.3). psalm_device_inventory lists 116 titled psalms and Ps 91 is not among them; pmarks selah covers 71 verses book-wide with 0 in Ps 91; of 65 K/Q verses book-wide the only one in Ps 90-91 is MT 90:8 - so nothing is owed by disclosure here. Confidence high is calibrated.

The arithmetic is right (91:3-10 is an eight-verse span, identity numbering) and the address is genuinely second-person at 91:3-8 and 91:10. The substrate evidence for holding 91:9 inside the span is not: MT 91:9 opens with a fresh independent second-person pronoun and then a first-person suffix that returns the speaker's own voice from 91:2 - the opposite of what the row's first signal asserts. That matters because 91:9 is precisely the rival seam the row rejects, and it carries the same verse-initial particle that opens the three seams accepted elsewhere in this psalm. The row's other claims check out: no superscription for Ps 91 and no selah anywhere in the psalm per pmarks, so the span-scoped absence statement in device_notes is accurate and check_marks is GREEN. The span may still be right - 91:9-10 do read as premise and result - but the stated warrant needs re-derivation from the pointed text before the rival is dismissed, and confidence medium is generous while it rests on a false signal.

reviews.reasoning: The quoted Hebrew is byte tier at its cited ref and the quote and gloss cover the same clause, but the grammatical warrant is wrong in both the rationale and the substrate signal: the plural noun for the angels cannot be the subject of the singular prefixed verb beside it, and the row's own gloss treats it as the object, as does WEB. The subject at 91:11 is the same implied third-person subject already made explicit in the parallel particle-clause at 91:3, so nothing grammatically new is introduced at 91:11 - what is new is the agent-object of the protection. The seam itself is not contested: the image shift is real and the following unit's voice change at 91:14 is byte-supported. device_notes' non-recurrence statement is true but unswept - that skeleton token occurs in 1 verse of Ps 91 (91:11; 4 verses book-wide) - which is worth a digit in the field rather than a separate challenge. Confidence medium is calibrated given the warrant is repairable without moving the span.

challenges.claim: The angels noun is the fronted object of a singular verb, not the span's grammatical subject, and the subject at 91:11 is the same third-person subject already explicit at 91:3, so the claim that 91:11 introduces a new grammatical subject is false.
challenges.evidence: Byte-tier splice from oshb:Ps.91.11 (= web:Ps.91.11): כִּ֣י מַ֭לְאָכָיו יְצַוֶּה לָּ֑ךְ; the noun מַ֭לְאָכָיו is plural while the verb יְצַוֶּה is a singular prefixed form, so the noun cannot be its subject. oshb:Ps.91.3 (= web:Ps.91.3) supplies that subject explicitly: כִּ֤י ה֣וּא יַ֭צִּֽילְךָ - same particle, explicit third-person singular pronoun, singular verb with a 2ms object suffix. WEB agrees with the object reading in both places: “For he will put his angels in charge of you,” (web:Ps.91.11) against “For he will deliver you from the snare of the fowler,” (web:Ps.91.3). The row's own gloss reads the noun as object, so rationale and substrate signal contradict the gloss beside them; the repair states a new protective agent, not a new subject.

reviews.reasoning: The span and its voice warrant are sound: divine first-person speech genuinely begins at 91:14 (כִּ֤י בִ֣י חָ֭שַׁק וַאֲפַלְּטֵ֑הוּ, oshb:Ps.91.14 = web:Ps.91.14, byte tier) and runs to the psalm's last verb (אַשְׂבִּיעֵ֑הוּ, oshb:Ps.91.16 = web:Ps.91.16), so the warrant does not depend on WEB's quotation marks, which are rendering-level punctuation - a useful cross-check, not the driver. WEB's bracketing is as described: “Because he has set his love on me, therefore I will deliver him.” (web:Ps.91.14) opens it and “I will satisfy him with long life, and show him my salvation.” (web:Ps.91.16) closes it at the psalm's end. The defect is the second substrate signal's contrast with the rest of the psalm, an unswept universal that fails on the psalm's second verse, where two first-person verbs stand. The accurate contrast is divine first-person speech, not first person as such - and the opening unit of this same psalm reads 91:2 as a first-person confession, so the two statements cannot both stand.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal contrasting the span's first-person verb with the third-person and second-person verbs of the rest of the psalm is falsified by 91:2, which carries two first-person verbs.

WEB renders them “I will say of Yahweh,” (web:Ps.91.2) and “my God, in whom I trust.” (web:Ps.91.2). The claim also carries no digit-bearing sweep for its rest-of-the-psalm scope; restated as divine first-person speech it survives, supported by the 1cs verbs at oshb:Ps.91.14, oshb:Ps.91.15 and oshb:Ps.91.16.
